name: GraphCanvas
intent: Themed node-and-edge canvas: dotted background, controls, optional minimap, and the house viewport defaults for a layered DAG.
when: A state machine, pipeline wiring, lineage DAG or ontology graph
Any surface where nodes and typed edges are the content
whenNot: A hierarchy that reads better as a tree -> use TreeRow
A chart of values rather than a graph of relations -> use Chart or TrendChart

chooseOver.because: Four canvases each re-typed the provider, background, controls and viewport defaults, and had already drifted — three padded fitView and one did not. This keeps them one surface while forwarding every ReactFlowProps so the domain stays with the caller.

requiredProviders: Wraps its own ReactFlowProvider unless withProvider is false

layout.note: layered adds smoothstep edges and fitView padding; free drops both.

onFitView.note: For a canvas that wants an animated re-fit.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Node and edge ids must be unique within one canvas.

children.description: Panels, overlays and legends rendered inside the canvas

states.layered: smoothstep edges and a padded fitView that frames the whole graph on mount.
states.free: No edge-type default and no fit padding — for a radial graph the user navigates.
states.withMiniMap: A pannable, zoomable minimap in the corner.

allowedPlacement: inside a fixed-height or min-h-0 flex container
forbiddenPlacement: a container with no resolved height — the canvas collapses to a 0px strip
minimalExample:
import {GraphCanvas} from "@corensystem/coren-ui/graph-canvas";

<GraphCanvas nodes={nodes} edges={edges} nodeTypes={NODE_TYPES} onNodeClick={select} />
evaluationCriteria: The xyflow attribution stays visible — MIT terms depend on it.
The canvas sits in a container with a resolved height.
A radial graph passes layout="free" rather than inheriting DAG defaults.

lineage.authoredBy: Extracted from the four xyflow canvases found in the missing-widgets template review (2026-08-25)

extracted: smoothstep edge default for layered DAGs (layout="free" opts out; the process state machine does)

lineage.supersedes: The inline ReactFlow surfaces in wc3-process-detail, wc3-pipeline-detail, wc3-lineage-data-view and wc3-graph-explorer-flow
notes: The four had already diverged: three passed fitViewOptions padding and wc3-graph-explorer-flow did not.
proOptions.hideAttribution stays false — @xyflow/react is MIT only while the credit shows.

colorMode is derived from the `dark` class Core toggles on <html> and passed to ReactFlow, which is the only supported way to reach React Flow's own `.react-flow.dark` chrome — node fill and border, edge stroke, Controls, MiniMap. A caller can still pin a canvas by passing colorMode itself. Added when the process state machine moved onto React Flow's built-in default node, which is otherwise white with a near-black border on a near-black page.

The canvas ground is React Flow's own --xy-background-color, set to the two values reactflow.dev's example theme (xy-theme.css) uses: #f7f9fb light, #101012 dark. It replaced a bg-muted/20 class, which beat the library's own background rule; setting their variable instead leaves that rule in charge and a caller can still override through `style`. The Background dots carry no colour prop or class — the dot fill reads --xy-background-pattern-dots-color-default (#91919a / #555), never currentColor, so the text-border class that used to sit there painted nothing.

It is the ONE DOOR to @xyflow/react. Alongside the component it re-exports everything a canvas page needs — Handle, Position, MarkerType, Panel, useNodesState, useEdgesState, useReactFlow, and the Node / Edge / NodeProps / EdgeProps / Connection / FinalConnectionState types — plus the stylesheet, loaded once from here and verified to survive the tsdown build. Nothing is renamed or wrapped: these ARE React Flow's primitives, and Core-sounding aliases would only make the next person open two files to find the real documentation. What the re-export buys is that one module owns the dependency, its version and its context, so a page cannot pick up a second copy or drift onto an API this canvas has not adopted. StateMachine names no third-party package because of it; the pipeline, lineage and ontology canvases still import xyflow directly and have not been migrated.

A SELECTED node carries a 2px primary ring and a soft lift, set as React Flow's own --xy-node-boxshadow-selected rather than a rule of ours, so the library still owns when the ring appears and on which element. Its default is 0.5px of near-black, which is readable on a white node and invisible on a tinted one. React Flow scopes the declaration to the built-in node type names, so it reaches a node registered under `default` and leaves canvases with fully custom node components alone; the same rule covers :focus-visible, so a keyboard user gets the identical ring. One consequence worth knowing: because React Flow shares one variable between .selected and :focus, a node deselected by clicking it a second time keeps the ring until focus moves.

showControls turns off React Flow's own Controls for a canvas whose surrounding chrome already owns zoom and fit — NodeGraph, which draws the ZoomTools row above it. Two fit buttons on one canvas is one too many.

usage: Use GraphCanvas to display structured data or visualizations. This component helps users understand and interact with complex information sets.

GraphCanvas is ideal for dashboards, reports, and data-heavy interfaces. Ensure data is presented clearly and consider responsive behavior for different screen sizes. Provide appropriate loading states for async data.

props.name: layout
props.description: `"layered"` (default) is a left-to-right or top-down DAG: orthogonal `smoothstep` edges and a padded `fitView` that frames the whole graph on mount. `"free"` is a radial or force-placed graph the user navigates — no edge-type default and no fit padding, since there is no lane structure to respect.

props.name: showMiniMap
props.description: Show the pannable/zoomable minimap. Off by default — see the note on `MiniMap` below.

props.name: showControls
props.description: Show React Flow's own zoom/fit `Controls`. On by default. Turn it off when the surrounding chrome already owns those actions — two fit buttons on one canvas is one too many.

props.name: children
props.description: Rendered inside the canvas, after the chrome — panels, overlays, legends.

props.name: withProvider
props.description: Wrap in a `ReactFlowProvider`. Set false when the caller already owns one. Default true.

anatomy.description: GraphCanvas is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
